IPTV vs Netflix in the UK: Which One Fits How You Watch?

Before you compare IPTV and Netflix, ask yourself one simple question: when you sit down to watch television, do you usually press play or tune in?

10 min read•Updated 4 August 2026
Feature-by-feature table2026 cost breakdownWho should choose what

If you prefer choosing a film, box set or original series whenever it suits you, Netflix — used by around six in ten UK households — is likely to feel familiar. If you still plan your evening around live television, scheduled channels, catch-up viewing or sport, IPTV may fit the way you watch more naturally.

The important thing to remember is that IPTV is simply television delivered through the internet, and its legality depends on whether the provider holds the correct rights to the content it offers. So you are not really choosing a universal winner; you are deciding whether your household needs on-demand entertainment, live television, or a combination of both that could cost less than a traditional pay-TV package.

What Netflix Actually Gives You

Netflix earns its place in your home by making an ordinary evening effortless: you open the app, continue the series you started last night, download something for a journey, or let its recommendations rescue you from the familiar "what should we watch?" debate. Its biggest originals — Stranger Things, The Crown, Wednesday, Squid Game and Bridgerton — still have the budgets, casts and cultural impact of major television events, while the wider catalogue gives you films, documentaries, international dramas and reliable comfort viewing in one polished app.

The limitation appears when you expect Netflix to replace an entire television package. Although it now carries selected live programming such as WWE, boxing, concerts and special events, it does not give you the everyday mix of BBC One, ITV1, rolling news, Sky Sports, TNT Sports or a full weekend of live football. You may never notice that gap if you mainly want a great film or box set waiting when you finally sit down, but if your viewing routine depends on regular live channels and broader sports coverage, Netflix becomes one excellent part of your setup rather than the whole solution.

What IPTV Gives You That Netflix Cannot

IPTV gives you something Netflix is not designed to provide: a full live television experience. With a properly licensed service, you can move between live channels, check a programme guide, catch up on missed shows and follow sport without opening several different apps.

For football fans, the difference is significant: during the 2026/27 Premier League season, at least 267 of the 380 matches will be shown live in the UK, with Sky Sports carrying at least 215 and TNT Sports showing 52, while Sky remains the UK home of Formula 1. An authorised IPTV package can bring that coverage together with BBC, ITV, Channel 4, Channel 5, regional channels, news, entertainment and an on-demand library — you can see the full IPTV UK channel list for what that looks like in practice.

One claim to check carefully

Be careful with providers claiming to show every Premier League match, because Saturday 3pm fixtures remain unavailable for legal broadcast in the UK during the blackout period.

Which Service Is Easier to Set Up?

Netflix usually takes only a few minutes to get running: download the app, sign in and choose a profile. IPTV may require a separate player, login details and an electronic programme guide before the channels appear correctly. Some providers complete the setup for you, while others send instructions for you to follow. Check whether your Smart TV, Fire TV Stick, phone or streaming box supports the required player — our device-by-device setup guide covers the common ones — and ask whether the player carries an additional fee.

Why Netflix Feels Easier to Trust

Netflix earns its advantage when you care less about huge content numbers and more about knowing exactly what will happen after you pay. Your subscription, billing, parental controls, accessibility settings and customer support all sit under one established service, while every Netflix Original has a recognised legal home rather than depending on a reseller, playlist or third-party programme guide. Ofcom found that 26% of viewers name Netflix as their first destination when looking for something to watch. You can change plans, cancel online and use a familiar account experience across supported devices without dealing with a separate reseller.

The Real Cost Comparison in 2026

Streaming bills rarely feel expensive at first; they grow one subscription at a time. Netflix currently costs £5.99 with adverts, £12.99 for Standard and £18.99 for Premium, while a flexible NOW Sports Month Membership costs £34.99. Pair Netflix Standard with NOW Sports and you reach £47.98 a month, or £575.76 a year, for Netflix entertainment and access to the Sky Sports channels carried by NOW.

Cost pressure is already changing household behaviour: Ofcom found that 13% of Netflix subscribers downgraded during the previous year, with 62% of them moving to the cheaper advert-supported tier.

By comparison, our 12-month Ultimate Plan is £49.99 paid upfront, an effective rate of about £4.17 a month. Adding Netflix Standard brings the average combined cost to roughly £17.16 a month. A low monthly figure only represents genuine value when the promised access remains stable, supported and legally authorised.

Should You Use IPTV and Netflix Together?

You do not need to force everyone in your home into the same viewing routine. One person may follow a Netflix drama while another watches live sport, the evening news or a programme airing at a fixed time. Ofcom reports that 69% of UK households subscribe to at least one of Netflix, Prime Video or Disney+, while 20% pay for all three, showing that using more than one service is already normal. Keeping Netflix and IPTV together makes sense when both are opened regularly and serve different people in your household.

Who Should Choose What?

Netflix only

You watch in your own time

Films, documentaries and series whenever it suits you, with a familiar app, offline downloads and straightforward billing. Enough on its own when live channels rarely form part of your week.

IPTV only

You watch on a schedule

Scheduled programmes, news, catch-up and regular live broadcasts matter more than Netflix exclusives. Focus on the channels your household genuinely watches rather than a provider’s total channel count.

Both together

Your household is split

Different viewing habits under one roof, with both services used every week. Review both regularly and cancel whichever one spends more time unopened than playing.

Before You Subscribe

Before paying for an IPTV plan, confirm the total upfront cost, subscription length and renewal price. Check how many screens can play at the same time, whether the player app costs extra and which channels or catch-up services are included. Read the refund terms, test playback during busy evening hours and ask the provider to explain its content and distribution rights.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does IPTV replace Netflix?+

Not completely. IPTV may cover scheduled channels, catch-up programmes and a separate on-demand library, but Netflix Originals remain tied to Netflix. Check your recent viewing history before cancelling.

Can I watch the Premier League on Netflix?+

No. Netflix carries selected live events, but it does not hold UK Premier League rights. Official coverage is available through licensed sports broadcasters. Saturday 3pm matches remain inside the UK broadcast blackout, so claims of authorised access to every fixture should be checked carefully.

Is IPTV cheaper than Netflix?+

It can be, but always check how the monthly figure is calculated. Our 12-month Ultimate Plan is £49.99 paid upfront, which works out at roughly £4.17 a month, while the 1-month Starter Plan is £14.99. Netflix starts at £5.99 per month and allows monthly cancellation, so a short IPTV plan and a Netflix subscription can cost about the same.

Do I need a TV Licence for IPTV or Netflix?+

You need a UK TV Licence when you watch programmes or events live through IPTV, Netflix or another streaming platform. A licence is also required whenever you use BBC iPlayer, including on-demand programmes. You do not need one when you only watch standard on-demand Netflix films and series and never use BBC iPlayer. The same rules apply on televisions, phones, tablets and laptops.

Can I use Netflix and IPTV on the same television?+

Usually, yes. Netflix and an IPTV player can run on the same compatible Smart TV or streaming device. App availability varies between television operating systems, so check whether your device supports the required IPTV player before subscribing. A Fire TV Stick or another streaming device may be needed when the television’s app store does not carry it.

Next step

Try It Before You Commit

Test the service on your own television and broadband before choosing a long-term plan. Open the channels you normally watch and check how quickly support responds.

Do not judge a trial by opening a few channels for ten minutes. Test the programme guide, catch-up, picture quality, device switching and playback during the hours when your household normally watches television. Choose a longer plan only when performance remains stable and the final payment terms are clear.
